title: When the Scholarship Sings
premise: Wren Sandoval, the meticulous statistician of her elite prep school's championship basketball team, has spent five years quietly documenting how boosters and coaches rig games — evidence she's too afraid to use. When a teacher pairs her with Theo Marchetti, the team's star player and her oldest enemy, for a semester project on institutional ethics, they stumble onto proof that the fix is bigger than either imagined: the championship itself is being sold. Forced into an uneasy alliance, Wren and Theo must decide whether to play along and gather proof, or blow up the season and their futures. In the end they expose the conspiracy at the state final — winning the game honestly while losing scholarships, friendships, and Wren's carefully guarded safety, but gaining something rarer: justice that costs what it should.
about_author: Coral Joubert is the pen name of a former high school debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers navigate institutions built to fail them. She writes from a small coastal town where the gym lights stay on late.

chapters.title: The Spreadsheet Doesn't Lie
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Opening at midseason, Wren runs game stats and notices the team's fouls cluster in impossible patterns whenever booster money is on the line. She locks the file away, as always. Emotional beat: dread disguised as competence; we see how much being careful costs her.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ms. Okafor announces semester partners for the civics capstone: Wren and Theo Marchetti, the star forward who humiliated her freshman year. Their first meeting in the library is acid and stale air. Beat: reluctant collision; two people who think they already know each other.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They negotiate a truce: Theo handles interviews, Wren handles data, no personal history discussed. But Theo lets slip he suspects his own minutes are being managed by someone off-court. Beat: first crack of shared suspicion.

chapters.title: The Booster Room
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo attends a 'donor appreciation' night to interview Coach Brandt and overhears a number — $40,000 — attached to a player's name that isn't his. He records eleven seconds before nearly getting caught. Beat: fear as adrenaline; the project stops being homework.

chapters.title: Eleven Seconds
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Theo plays her the recording. Her five years of spreadsheets suddenly have a voice attached. They argue about going to the principal; Wren's caution versus Theo's fury. Beat: alliance forged out of mutual alarm rather than trust.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV flashback chapter. We learn why she's so careful: her older brother took a fall for a coach years ago and lost everything. Beat: vulnerability; the reader finally understands her armor.

chapters.title: The Project That Isn't
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They build a fake capstone on 'institutional ethics' as cover while mapping the real network: Brandt, an athletic director, and a betting syndicate. First near-miss when a teammate almost finds their files. Beat: conspiratorial intimacy deepening into friendship.

chapters.title: Deliberate Misses
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On court, Theo realizes he's being ordered to shave points via coded substitutions. He complies once and hates himself. Beat: complicity; power corrupting from the inside of its victim.

chapters.title: Ms. Okafor's Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Okafor, sharp-eyed, tells Wren that two students tried this six years ago and were 'managed' out. She neither helps nor stops them — just says, 'Decide what you can live with.' Beat: moral vertigo; the cost becomes concrete.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Talks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Best friend Devi figures out what they're doing and wants in; Wren refuses, Theo overrules. Devi's carelessness draws attention from the athletic director. Beat: hubris; the circle widens and weakens.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The AD calls Wren in for a friendly chat about 'college recommendations' — an offer wrapped around a threat. She smiles and lies perfectly, then shakes afterward. Beat: survival price paid in small humiliations.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Devi obtains a photo of the actual payout ledger. Names, dates, amounts — including Theo's own name with a figure beside it he never received. Beat: betrayal inside betrayal; Theo learns he was collateral, not partner.

chapters.title: Split
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo wants to go public immediately; Wren insists they need the chain complete or it'll be buried like her brother's case was. They fight viciously and split the work. Beat: lowest point of the alliance; pride vs. strategy.

chapters.title: Devi Pays
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Devi is suspended on fabricated plagiarism charges — clearly retaliation. Guilt lands hard on both leads. Beat: consequences arrive; the abstract danger becomes a person they love, hurt.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Dark
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren and Theo reconcile in the empty gym at midnight, trading truths instead of tactics. Theo admits he's terrified of losing his scholarship future; Wren admits she's terrified of mattering. Beat: tenderness; stakes become personal and romantic tension surfaces.

chapters.title: The Chain Complete
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the money through a shell charity, they connect the syndicate to a school board member. The evidence is whole — but also damning enough that going public will torch the whole team's season. Beat: cold clarity; victory and destruction are the same act.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Someone tips off Brandt that copies exist. Theo's locker is searched, his phone cloned. They realize the only safe move is to move first — during the state final, in front of cameras. Beat: ticking clock engaged; no retreat remains.

chapters.title: State Final, First Half
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Game day. The syndicate's fix is in motion; Theo must play well enough to be believable but the script says lose. Wren watches from the scorer's table with a drive containing everything. Beat: unbearable suspense; every possession double-loaded.

chapters.title: Halftime Decision
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Down nine at half, Theo breaks the script and plays to win. In the locker room tunnel, Wren must choose: release the file now, mid-game, or never. She sends it to the press, the board, and Okafor simultaneously. Beat: point of no return; courage as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Championship That Matters
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo wins the game honestly in overtime as phones light up courtside; the AD tries to cut the feed, but too many eyes have seen. Brandt is escorted out under the scoreboard. Beat: climax; triumph and exposure fused into one moment.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hearings, vacated titles, teammates who won't speak to them, Theo's scholarship offers evaporating one by one. Devi is reinstated; Okafor testifies. Beat: the bill arrives; justice is real and it hurts exactly as much as promised.

chapters.title: What Sings
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue. Months later: Wren publishes the full statistical study under her own name; Theo walks on at a smaller college. In the empty gym, they hear the old scoreboard hum — the scholarship didn't save them, but the truth did. Beat: bittersweet resolution; the price was paid, and it was worth it.
